script:
Roth or traditional 401(k)?
Most people get this wrong, but here's exactly how to choose.
A traditional 401(k) takes pre-tax dollars, lowering your taxable income today.
But in retirement, every dollar you withdraw is taxed as ordinary income.
A Roth 401(k) uses after-tax dollars, so there's no tax break today.
Instead, your qualified withdrawals in retirement are completely tax-free.
Plus, Roth 401(k)s have no required minimum distributions during your lifetime.
Here's the worked dollar example.
Say you invest five thousand dollars.
At a seven percent return over thirty years, that grows to thirty-eight thousand sixty-one dollars.
In a traditional account, paying a twenty-four percent tax at withdrawal takes nine thousand one hundred and thirty-four dollars.
You walk away with twenty-eight thousand nine hundred and twenty-seven dollars.
In a Roth, you keep that full thirty-eight thousand sixty-one dollars tax-free.
How you choose comes down to two questions.
One: will your tax bracket be higher now, or in retirement?
If your bracket will be higher in retirement, Roth wins because you lock in the lower rate today.
If you're in peak earning years and your bracket will drop, traditional wins because you take the deduction at your highest rate.
Two: do you need cash in your paycheck right now?
If money is tight, traditional gives you that immediate tax relief.
If you're not sure, you can even split your contributions between both accounts.
Do your own research, but let me know: are you team Roth or traditional?
And if you're looking to grow your net worth, follow me.
